messages:
alex: Quick question — for the autofallback rollout canary, do we prioritise error-rate triggers over latency spikes? Trying to map operator expectations.

maria: My vote is error-rate first. Latency can be noisy; we should only fallback on sustained latency above SLO for X minutes. :thinking:

tyler: Agree on signal hierarchy. Also want to avoid oscillation if latency degrades briefly. We discussed a hysteresis window (e.g., 3m) in the doc.

sam: Is there a plan for soft vs hard degrade? We have soft_degrade (reduced model size) and hard_degrade (route to fallback model). Operators need clear signage in the console.

jane: Can we put the policy schema in the console so SREs can preview behavior? e.g., show simulated traces when editing thresholds.

alex: good call. Example minimal policy snippet I shared in the design review, repeating here for clarity:

```json
{
  "name": "canary-autofallback",
  "triggers": [
    {"type": "error_rate", "window": "1m", "threshold": 0.05, "mode": "hard_degrade"},
    {"type": "latency_p95", "window": "5m", "threshold": 1200, "mode": "soft_degrade"}
  ],
  "hysteresis": {"grace_period": "3m", "cooldown": "5m"},
  "audit": {"enabled": true, "sample_rate": 0.1}
}
```

maria: That looks reasonable. A couple notes: error_rate should be broken down by class (client 4xx vs server 5xx) and by route. We don't want user typing errors to trigger platform fallback.

tyler: +1 separate counters. Also think we need a separate "backend_error" signal vs generic error_rate. backend_error -> immediate hard_degrade. client_errors -> ignore unless spike is massive.

sam: On the audit side, can we capture the decision trace id and policy snapshot so rollback is reproducible? e.g., audit payload = {policy_id, snapshot, decision_ts, input_signals, selected_action}.

jane: UX asks: show audit events inline in the rollout timeline and allow operators to replay the simulation with the exact snapshot. We already have the playback infra; just need a small API surface.

alex: Implementation note: runtime will evaluate triggers in priority order to avoid conflicting actions. We'll expose a priority field on triggers so console can visualise execution order.

maria: How will we expose "soft_degrade" effect? Should be explicit: reduced model size, reduced beam, or cached response? Need preset templates in console.

tyler: Let's ship two templates: "latency_saver" (reduce model to quantized variant + batch size tweak) and "availability_saver" (route to cached responses or fallback model). Templates should list expected unit cost delta and success criteria.

sam: Audit sampling: default 10% is fine, but for first-10% of canary traffic we should sample 100% for the first 30 minutes. Operators need a way to bump sampling.

jane: UI microcopy: show a red banner when policy executed with exact reason "backend_error spike" and link to replay. Also allow an "annotate decision" field so oncall can leave context.

alex: Ops question — if policy triggers and rollback happens automatically, do we send an incident notif? I think yes but only for hard_degrade. Soft_degrade -> info channel. Thoughts?

maria: Agreed. Hard_degrade should create a brief incident with minimal paging (team oncall) and include the decision trace.

tyler: Edge case: rapid flapping between models. Hysteresis + escalation cap (max 1 hard_degrade per 30m) will help. Add that to policy schema: rate_limit: {"hard_degrade": "30m"}.

sam: I'll add a small proposal PR to the runtime repo: implement trigger priority, per-trigger rate limits, and audit snapshoting.

jane: I'll wire up the console mockups to include templates, the policy editor preview, and the replay button. Will ping for a design review tomorrow. :calendar:

sre-bot: deploy-bot: canary policy "canary-autofallback" created by alex at 1769001111 — sampling=10% initial.

alex: thanks all — aim to start canary rollout tomorrow 0800 PT. If anyone has last-minute blocking concerns post here or ping me directly. :thumbsup:
